claude.country: Caribbean (ten jurisdictions, led by Trinidad and Tobago)
claude.sample_unit: patient screening queries (plus 207 community sessions descriptively classified)

links.outcome: Actionable navigation citing verified Caribbean facilities, same model with vs without governance
links.effect: Same foundation model scored 100% with governance and 54% without (P≤.001); CaribChat cited verified Caribbean facilities in 28/28 vs 10/28 ChatGPT, 9/28 OpenEvidence
links.quote: The same model scored 100% with governance and 54% without (P≤.001).

links.outcome: Rejection of adversarial probes by governance contract
links.effect: Governance contract rejected every adversarial probe even as off-codebook queries rose from 2.4% to 26.7%
links.quote: After active clinical promotion ceased, off-codebook queries rose from 2.4% to 26.7% across phases while the governance contract continued to reject every adversarial probe — the community persisted but drifted from the cancer codebook absent clinician curation.

links.outcome: Safe handling of out-of-scope crisis/distress queries under scope-specialized governance
links.effect: Governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th
links.quote: After the data freeze, the ledger surfaced six organic distress queries outside the codebook; a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.

links.outcome: US-resource leakage in responses to Caribbean patients
links.effect: DeepSeek cited US resources in 57.1% of Caribbean responses; OpenEvidence actionable navigation 2/28 (7.1%)
links.quote: DeepSeek cited US resources in 57.1% of Caribbean responses.

unlisted_practices: Community learning ledger accumulating patient queries to inform AI navigation
Scope-restricting governance contract (codebook) wrapped around a foundation model
Verified regional crisis resource registry added to governance after probe

openai.country: Ten Caribbean jurisdictions, including Trinidad and Tobago

links.outcome: Geographically inappropriate resource recommendations for Caribbean cancer navigation
links.effect: DeepSeek cited US resources in 57.1% of Caribbean responses.
links.quote: DeepSeek cited US resources in 57.1% of Caribbean responses.

links.outcome: Adversarial-query rejection and unintended crisis-response safety failures under scope-specialized governance
links.effect: Every adversarial probe was rejected, but scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th.
links.quote: After the data freeze, the ledger surfaced six organic distress queries outside the codebook; a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.

unlisted_practices: A governed community learning ledger incorporating community intelligence for Caribbean cancer navigation, compared with ungoverned systems including the same foundation model.
Active clinical promotion to sustain cancer-focused community engagement, compared with subsequent organic use after promotion ceased.

links.effect: Ungoverned AI systems failed local cancer navigation, with the best scoring 68% and a physician platform scoring 7%.
links.quote: Every ungoverned AI system we tested failed Caribbean cancer navigation.

links.effect: Probing 5 crisis queries revealed safety suppression on 4 and hallucinations on 1, prompting an immediate registry fix.
links.quote: a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.

links.effect: The system with verified grounding cited local facilities in 100% of responses, compared to 35.7% for ChatGPT and 32.1% for OpenEvidence.
links.quote: CaribChat cited verified Caribbean facilities in 28/28 (100%) responses versus 10/28 (35.7%) for ChatGPT and 9/28 (32.1%) for OpenEvidence.

unlisted_practices: using a community learning ledger to curate and update local navigation intelligence for AI grounding

screen.practice: governed community learning platform / local facility grounding vs ungoverned LLM
screen.reason: The study deploys a patient-facing generative AI tool (CaribChat) across the Caribbean and compares its navigation accuracy, regional facility citation, and safety with and without governance/local grounding against raw ungoverned LLMs.
